fragments.text: Distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, my name is Ilesh Kratuna, I am a use activist to the campaign to stop killer robots in Hungary. Today, I will talk about the furthest end of automation and how to prevent it from devastating the world. The global market of artificial intelligence is expected to grow from $150 billion in 2023 to $1.3 trillion in 2030 at an annual growth rate of over 35 percent. Artificial intelligence that is using algorithms and machine learning to recognize patterns and imitate human intelligence is on its way to becoming a key factor in our changing global structures. An emerging technology that would help us solve our biggest problems as humanity or become our biggest problem.

fragments.text: The civil society, together with thousands of experts, have raised their voice against the development and use of killer robots. Yet, over 10 years of debate in the committee on the convention on certain conventional weapons did not lead to a meaningful result, as some countries blocked human dignity that is needed to move forward. Alongstanding solution could be an international convention, whereby states would set boundaries to the application of AI in weapons systems and establish a general standard of meaningful human control in weapons with autonomous capacities. At the first committee of this year's session of the United Nations General Assembly in October, a draft resolution, table by Austria, aims to address legal, ethical, humanitarian and security challenges raised by fully autonomous weapons.
